(d) the Defendant opposite party Nos. 02, 47 & 48 appeared in the suit on different dates and contested the same by filing separate written statements, denying all the material allegations contending inter alia that previously the Suit land was vested to the Government and subsequently suit land was partitioned and Swarnamoyee Devi owned as Zaminder and the suit land was registered in D Registered as new Touzi No. 16495; some of the defendants opposite parties including the defendant/ opposite party Nos. 02, 47 & 48 also claiming that the predecessor-in-interest got the suit land by permanent settlement from the Swarnamoyee Devi; thereafter suit land with other contagious land was auctioned for non-payment of lease money; the predecessors of the defendant/ opposite parties Moulavi Abul Fazal Mohammad and others acquired 16 Bigha 01 Kattha 03 Chatak land including the suit land of Touzi No. 16495 of the Dhaka Collectorate Mouja Sukrabad by way of purchase in Certificate Case No. 318 in the year 1935-1936 for valuable consideration and obtained Khas possession thereof; the aforesaid touzi No. 16495 was belong to Swarnamoyee Divi; the original Zamindari touzi being No. 5846 comprising of 6 (six) C.S. Khatians being Nos. 63, 66, 60, 62, 64 and 67 in which total area of land in plot Nos. 81 & 82 was 2.19 acres; the said Zamindari Touzi was later on divided and separate Touzi being No. 16495 of Swarnamoyee Devi was created; defendant- opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 further claiming that the property of Touzi No. 5846 of Mouza Sukrabad Comprising of 11 C.S. plots including C.S. Plot Nos. 81 and 82 (which includes the suit land to the extent of 1.03 acres of land) was acquired by the predecessor in interest of the Defendant-opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 by way of purchase in certificate case No. 318 of 1935-1936 and the said predecessor in interest Moulovi Abul Fazal Mohammad obtaining actual physical possession of the properties belonging to the predecessor in interest of the defendant opposite party nos. 47 & 48 were Requisitioned under Section 3 of the East Bengal ( Emergency) Requisition of property Act. 1948 (E.B Act XIII of 1948) by notification; thereafter the said land was Requisitioned by Government letter being No. 2620 of dated 15.08.1956 in favour of the said predecessor in interest Moulvi Abul Fazal and his brothers of the defendant Opposite party Nos. 47 & 48; the predecessors of the Defendants- opposite parties were taken award money as Awardee; later on, the concerning office of the Government has issued a latter and directed to deposit development cost of Rs. 8,620 to the Government which were taken earlier; the said Abul Fazal Mohammad in compliance with the direction of the Government deposited the said amount to the 

 State Bank of Pakistan, Dhaka by Treasury Challan No. 38, dated 23.08.1956 and the said fact was intimated to the Government by letter dated 25.08.1956; defendant-opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 further claiming that the said predecessor in interest of the Defendant Opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 while owning and possessing the said properties including the said property after the whole sale acquisition under East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 during S.A. Operation the said property including the suit property was recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 284 being plot No. 169 in the name of said Haji Abul Fazal Mohammad and his brothers as co-sharers as per their respective shares and was finally published without any objection whatsoever from any corner including the defendants/ opposite parties or their predecessor in office; thereafter the heirs and successors of the said Haji Abul Fazal Mohammad and his co sharers, while they were owning and possessing the said property including the suit property and the same during R.S. operation it was correctly recorded in their names in R.S. Khatian No.991 being R.S. plot No. 680 and it 681 and was finally published ; defendant- opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 further claiming that the Defendant opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 are the rightful owners in possession of the suit property to the extent of 784 Ajutangsha i.e 4 Kattha 12 chatak well demarcated land with specific boundaries appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 284 of plot No. 169 and R.S. Khatian No. 991 of plot No. 680,681 by way of purchase from its rightful owners in possession, who by way of inheritance and thereafter by amicable partition dated 15.06 1990 acquired the same; defendant opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 after purchase of the said property mutated their names in the Government Tahsil office and paid rents to the Government and also they after obtaining sanction of plan from the RAM( an investing huge amount of money constructed multistoried, puccas building in the said land and mutated their names in the Tax Assessment Register of the Dhaka City Corporation and obtained New Holding being No. 19 Dhanmondi R/A, Road No. 13 and paid Municipal Taxes to the City Corporation regularly. The defendants/ opposite parties also brought Electric, Gas, Was a connection and paid bill and charges in their names regularly; during recent Mohanagar Jarip their names were recorded up to the Tasdik stage but after final publication it was found that their properties has been wrongly recorded in the names of government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Land Reforms Board, Ministry of Land. The Defendant opposite party Nos. 47 & 48 shall take necessary legal steps in the appropriate forum against the said wrong recording in the Mohanagar Jarip. It need be mentioned here that the plaintiff’s petitioners filed several objection cases under section 30 & Appeals under Section 31 of the East Bengal State acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 being Appeal case Nos. 31651, 31657, 31658, 31659, 31660, 31661, 31662, 31663, 31664, 31665, 31666, 31667, 31668, 31669, 31670 and 31671, 31672, 31673, 31674, 31675, 3176, 31677, 31678, 31679, 31680, 31681, 31682, 31683, 31684 against several defendants regarding the suit property and those objection cases under section 30 were rejected and Appeals under Section 31 were also rejected on contest and the recording in the name of the land owners defendants/ Opposite parties were upheld; in the manner as stated the defendants opposite parties are the rightful owners in possession of their self acquired properties including the suit property by declaring and exercising every act of ownerships and possession openly, continuously, uninterruptedly and adversely against all including the defendants/opposite parties for long more than 60 years and the statuary period of limitation; the plaintiffs petitioners/ defendants have or had no semblance of any right, title, interest and possession over the property belonging to the defendants/ opposite parties including the suit property; the plaintiffs petitioners with malafide object of illegal gain or corrupt income generating filed the present vexatious suit against the defendants/ opposite parties only of making and harassing the defendant/ opposite parties by creating unwarranted pressure of litigation; the plaintiffs petitioners have no locus-standi to file the present suit against the defendant opposite parties nor they are entitled to any legal character or legal right to bring such a suit against the defendant opposite parties. The plaintiffs petitioners having not disclosed any cause of action or specific point of time of entering into possession by the defendants/opposite parties and also the suit land being totally vague, indefinite, unidentifiable and unspecified and as such the plaintiffs petitioners are not in law and equity are entitled to any decree as prayed for and as such the suit should be dismissed with compensatory costs in favour of the defendants. 

 (L) "The learned Additional Attorney General while making his submission in favour of the leave petitioner found it difficult to support the leave petitioner, since confronted with the gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 showing acquisition of rent receiving interest under Section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in respect of the lands covered by Monza Raza Bazar under J.L. No. 2 and the gazette notification dated 29.02.1956 showing acquisition and vesting of the lands, in respect of which the rent receiving interest have been acquired under Section 43(2), 46 C an 46E(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950 in favour of the Government." 

 Before enactment of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950 there was Zamindary system in the Land Administration and Zamindar had two types of property, one projabli property i.e. land settled to the projas subject to payment of rent to the Zamindar and another, the khas property i.e. the property remained in possession of the Zamindar like his own house, garden, ponds etc.; in the projabili property though the Zamindar had only rent receiving interest but in the name of realization of that interest/rent from the projas, the servants under the Zamindar (Paik Peyada) usually oppressed the projas/raiyats which shocked the then political leaders and social reformer for the abolishing the Zamindari System; those political leaders and social reformer promised to the general public that if the country is liberated from British Rule they would abolish the Zamindari system and the projas under the Zamindar won Id be upgraded as Malik (owner) from the status of Projas; 

 13. Accordingly, when the India was divided in the year 1947, the erstwhile Government of the Province of East Pakistan for abolishing the Zamindari system declaring the projas rights and title as owners had enacted the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950; 

 14. The provincial Government for giving effect the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in respect of the projabili property of the Za m i nda rim n t receiver remained under the management and custody of the court of Wards, the Government of the 

 “If the rent-receiving interests of a ward in ally estate under the charge of the Court are acquired under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, then, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, the remaining properties of such ward including khas lands under the charge and shall be managed in accordance with the provisions of this Act, as if such ward were a disqualified proprietor of an estate." 

 "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950 (E.B. Act No. XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Order No. Ill of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders, passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain, and no person shall bring, any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

 "It is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs. The province of East Pakistan decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiky vs. The province of East Pakistan that on the publication of the notification under section 3, of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all rent-receiving interests including that of debater and waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government." 

 In 1963 notifications u/s 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquiring of all interests other than those already acquired under section 3 of the Act, completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act, All the notifications have been published in the official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact is that the Bangladesh (Legal proceedings) (Third) Order, 1972 (P.O. 90 of 1972) was promulgated on 3rd August, 1972. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment-roll. President's Order No. 90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications, etc. pending in any court against the Government of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B . Ordinance No. III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property make there under is challenged in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction, etc. passed in such suits, appeals, etc. shall cease to have any effect and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question. 

 On the coming into operation of P.O. 90 of 1972 notwithstanding any other earlier view of law on the subject, a pending proceeding which is sought to be instituted challenging or calling in question the acquisition of any property under any of the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall abate and no proceedings shall be instituted in any Court. 

 "There can be no denying the fact that the plaintiffs sought to challenge the acquisition of their Hats and Bazars made under the general notification dated 02.04.1956 issued under section 3(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and so it is directly hit by President's Order No. 90 of 1972, which gives a clear mandate of law that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Ordinance No. III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suits, appeals applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no Court shall entered and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal, applications or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

 26. It is admitted facts that at the time of the abolishing the Zamindari system the erstwhile East Pakistan Government had enacted the law namely: "The East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950." 

 So, it is also revealed and admitted that the suit property was not khas property of the Jamindar, rather, admittedly it was projabili property; So, diming plaintiff declaration of right, titles and recovery of khas possession over the suit land are none but the Court of Wards is clearly against the provision of law of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in as much as under the provision of P.O. 90 of 1972 as the suit C.S. Khatian No. 63 and 66. 

 27. We have gone through the case law as well as the provision of law of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and P.O. No. 90 of 1972 as cited herein above then it would be crystal clear that the plaintiff filed the suit by challenging the acquisition of the property as a Court of Wards in violation of the provisions of Sections (3) A, 4 of the SAT Act-1950 read with Section 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act,1879 (Act No. X of 1951) and P.O. 90 of 1972.
